quests.hint: The list a server hands you so you can decide what to eat.
quests.explanation: 'Bring the menu' and 'look at the menu' both sound natural here. 'Set menu' means a fixed selection at a fixed price.
quests.textToSpeak: The waiter brought us the ___ and recommended the fish of the day.
quests.correctAnswer: The waiter brought us the menu and recommended the fish of the day.

quests.hint: What you do the moment you tell the waiter your choice.
quests.explanation: Order works as both verb ('I'd like to order') and noun ('take our order'). 'Ready to order?' is what servers ask before writing anything down.
quests.textToSpeak: Are you ready to ___, or do you need a few more minutes to decide?
quests.correctAnswer: Are you ready to order, or do you need a few more minutes to decide?

quests.hint: The sweet course that comes right after the main meal.
quests.explanation: Dessert is the standard word for a sweet course; 'pudding' is a common informal alternative in British English.
quests.textToSpeak: After the main course, we shared a chocolate cake for ___.
quests.correctAnswer: After the main course, we shared a chocolate cake for dessert.

quests.hint: The proof of payment you show before getting on a train or plane.
quests.explanation: 'Buy a ticket' and 'book a ticket' both work. A 'return ticket' takes you there and back; a 'single' only goes one way.
quests.textToSpeak: You need to buy a ___ before you can board the train to London.
quests.correctAnswer: You need to buy a ticket before you can board the train to London.

quests.hint: The official document that proves your identity and nationality abroad.
quests.explanation: 'Bring your passport' is essential travel advice. 'Passport control' is the checkpoint you pass through at any international border.
quests.textToSpeak: Do not forget to bring your ___ when travelling to another country.
quests.correctAnswer: Do not forget to bring your passport when travelling to another country.

quests.hint: Everything you pack into suitcases and bags for a trip.
quests.explanation: Luggage is uncountable — say 'a piece of luggage,' never 'a luggage.' 'Baggage' means exactly the same thing.
quests.textToSpeak: The airline allows each passenger to bring one piece of hand ___.
quests.correctAnswer: The airline allows each passenger to bring one piece of hand luggage.

quests.hint: The prediction that tells you whether to grab a coat or sunglasses.
quests.explanation: 'Weather forecast' is the standard term; 'check the forecast' is how most people describe looking it up before heading out.
quests.textToSpeak: According to the weather ___, it will be warm and dry all week long.
quests.correctAnswer: According to the weather forecast, it will be warm and dry all week long.

quests.hint: The number that tells you exactly how hot or cold it is outside.
quests.explanation: 'The temperature drops' or 'rises' — these are the everyday way to say it. We measure it in degrees Celsius or Fahrenheit.
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ dropped below zero overnight and there was frost on all the cars.
quests.correctAnswer: The temperature dropped below zero overnight and there was frost on all the cars.

quests.hint: A waterproof jacket you'd reach for on a wet, grey day.
quests.explanation: Raincoat is one word. 'Wellies' (wellington boots) often gets paired with it, especially in British English.
quests.textToSpeak: She wore her ___ and wellies because the weather outside was terrible.
quests.correctAnswer: She wore her raincoat and wellies because the weather outside was terrible.

quests.hint: Any physical activity you do on purpose to stay fit.
quests.explanation: 'Get exercise' or 'do exercise' both work as general phrases; specific activities like 'go running' use their own verb instead.
quests.textToSpeak: Regular ___ is one of the best things you can do for your long-term health.
quests.correctAnswer: Regular exercise is one of the best things you can do for your long-term health.

quests.hint: Moving through water using your arms and legs, usually for fitness or fun.
quests.explanation: 'Go swimming' follows the same pattern as 'go running' or 'go shopping' — 'go' plus an '-ing' activity.
quests.textToSpeak: She goes ___ three times a week to stay fit and reduce her stress levels.
quests.correctAnswer: She goes swimming three times a week to stay fit and reduce her stress levels.

quests.hint: The place with weights and machines that people pay to use regularly.
quests.explanation: 'Join the gym' and 'go to the gym' are the two phrases you'll need most. 'Gym' is short for 'gymnasium.'
quests.textToSpeak: He joined the local ___ and started training five days a week.
quests.correctAnswer: He joined the local gym and started training five days a week.

quests.hint: Step-by-step instructions for cooking a particular dish.
quests.explanation: 'Follow a recipe' is the phrase to remember. 'A recipe for disaster' is a fun idiom meaning a plan likely to go badly wrong!
quests.textToSpeak: She followed a simple online ___ to make the most amazing chocolate cake.
quests.correctAnswer: She followed a simple online recipe to make the most amazing chocolate cake.

quests.hint: The individual items you combine to make a dish.
quests.explanation: 'Have the ingredients ready' is common before starting to cook. The word is almost always used in the plural.
quests.textToSpeak: Before you start cooking, make sure you have all the ___ ready to go.
quests.correctAnswer: Before you start cooking, make sure you have all the ingredients ready to go.

quests.hint: The appliance you heat up to bake or roast food inside.
quests.explanation: 'Preheat the oven' means warming it up before you put food in — a step almost every baking recipe requires.
quests.textToSpeak: Preheat the ___ to 180 degrees before putting in the biscuits.
quests.correctAnswer: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees before putting in the biscuits.

quests.hint: A scheduled time to see someone, like a doctor or dentist.
quests.explanation: 'Make an appointment' and 'book an appointment' both work. 'Miss an appointment' usually means you'll need to reschedule.
quests.textToSpeak: I need to make a dental ___ for a routine check-up as soon as possible.
quests.correctAnswer: I need to make a dental appointment for a routine check-up as soon as possible.

quests.hint: The date or time by which something absolutely must be finished.
quests.explanation: 'Meet a deadline' means finishing on time; 'miss a deadline' means finishing late. 'A tight deadline' means very little time to work with.
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ for submitting the report is Friday at five o'clock sharp.
quests.correctAnswer: The deadline for submitting the report is Friday at five o'clock sharp.

quests.hint: A plan showing what's happening and when.
quests.explanation: 'Check your schedule' and 'a busy schedule' are worth learning together. The British pronunciation differs from the American one, though the spelling stays the same.
quests.textToSpeak: Please check your ___ and let me know when you are available to meet.
quests.correctAnswer: Please check your schedule and let me know when you are available to meet.

quests.hint: The yearly celebration of the day someone was born.
quests.explanation: 'Birthday party' and 'happy birthday' are the two phrases you'll use constantly. Birthday is always one word.
quests.textToSpeak: She baked a special cake for her son's ___ party on Saturday afternoon.
quests.correctAnswer: She baked a special cake for her son's birthday party on Saturday afternoon.

quests.hint: Something you give someone to mark a special occasion.
quests.explanation: Present and 'gift' mean the same thing, though 'gift' sounds slightly more formal. 'Wrap a present' is a classic pre-celebration task.
quests.textToSpeak: He bought her a beautiful necklace as a ___ for their anniversary.
quests.correctAnswer: He bought her a beautiful necklace as a present for their anniversary.

quests.hint: What you do to mark a happy occasion or achievement.
quests.explanation: 'Celebrate an achievement' or 'celebrate a birthday' — the verb works with almost any happy event worth marking.
quests.textToSpeak: The whole team went out to dinner to ___ completing the difficult project.
quests.correctAnswer: The whole team went out to dinner to celebrate completing the difficult project.

quests.hint: The amount of money you'd need to hand over to buy something.
quests.explanation: 'The price of' something is how most speakers say it. 'Price tag' refers to the actual label showing that number.
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ of the jacket was far too high, so she decided not to buy it.
quests.correctAnswer: The price of the jacket was far too high, so she decided not to buy it.

quests.hint: The small piece of paper proving you paid for something.
quests.explanation: 'Keep your receipt' is common advice for returns. Note the silent 'p' — it's pronounced 'ree-seet,' not 'reh-sipt.'
quests.textToSpeak: Always keep your ___ in case you need to return or exchange the item.
quests.correctAnswer: Always keep your receipt in case you need to return or exchange the item.

quests.hint: Getting your money back after returning something faulty.
quests.explanation: 'Get a refund' or 'give a refund' — one from the customer's side, one from the shop's. 'A full refund' means every penny back.
quests.textToSpeak: The shop gave her a full ___ because the item was faulty when it arrived.
quests.correctAnswer: The shop gave her a full refund because the item was faulty when it arrived.

quests.hint: A dull, throbbing pain right inside your skull.
quests.explanation: 'Have a headache' is the natural choice here. 'A splitting headache' describes an especially painful one.
quests.textToSpeak: She had a terrible ___ and had to lie down in a quiet, darkened room.
quests.correctAnswer: She had a terrible headache and had to lie down in a quiet, darkened room.

quests.hint: What a doctor prescribes to help treat an illness.
quests.explanation: Medicine is usually uncountable: 'take medicine,' 'some medicine.' 'A medicine' only works when referring to one specific type or brand.
quests.textToSpeak: The doctor prescribed some ___ and told her to get plenty of rest.
quests.correctAnswer: The doctor prescribed some medicine and told her to get plenty of rest.

quests.hint: The traditional British name for a shop that sells medicine.
quests.explanation: Chemist's takes an apostrophe because it's short for 'chemist's shop.' 'Pharmacy' is the more international equivalent.
quests.textToSpeak: You can buy that particular cream without a prescription from any local ___.
quests.correctAnswer: You can buy that particular cream without a prescription from any local chemist's.

quests.hint: Step-by-step guidance for finding your way to a place.
quests.explanation: 'Give directions' and 'ask for directions' are the go-to phrases. The word is almost always plural in this sense.
quests.textToSpeak: Could you give me ___ to the nearest underground station from here?
quests.correctAnswer: Could you give me directions to the nearest underground station from here?

quests.hint: A point where a road branches off to the left or right.
quests.explanation: 'Take a turning' is common in giving directions. 'Turn left' uses the verb form instead of this noun.
quests.textToSpeak: Take the second ___ on the left and the hotel is on your right.
quests.correctAnswer: Take the second turning on the left and the hotel is on your right.

quests.hint: A circular junction where traffic flows around a central island.
quests.explanation: Roundabout is common across the UK; Americans usually call the same thing a 'traffic circle.'
quests.textToSpeak: Go straight through the ___ and then follow the signs for the town centre.
quests.correctAnswer: Go straight through the roundabout and then follow the signs for the town centre.
